newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures surge late, end up on storm fears.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures surge late, end up on storm fears.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, helped by a late wave of short covering on news of a Louisiana gas line leak and concerns about a Caribbean storm.
November surged 16.4 cents to close at $2.464 per million British thermal units. December settled 15.4 cents higher at $2.634. Other deferreds ended up by 1.6 to 12.0 cents.

"We were up on short covering on the storm, weather revisions and the leak," said one Midwest trader, adding prices were likely to retreat sharply once the storm passes unless colder weather kicks in.

A tropical depression in the western Caribbean, with winds of about 35 mph, was expected to strengthen over the next 24 hours, as it gradually turned toward Cuba at about nine mph, the National Hurricane Center said. At 1700 EDT, it was located about 470 miles south of Havana.
Traders said news Tuesday of a Tennessee Gas line leak in Louisiana which cut 250 mmcfd of secondary services for up to three days also helped drive the market.
But while milder weather later this week and next could soon pressure cash and futures, traders said another cold front later in the month may limit any pullback.
Technically, traders still saw November support in the mid-$2.20s and then in the mid-teens. Resistance was now pegged at $2.50 and then at the recent high of $2.59.
Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly Tuesday to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes firmed more than five cents to the low-to-mid teens.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip jumped 5.1 cents to $2.223.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled 1.5 cents higher at $1.055, while deferreds closed up one to 2.5 cents.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but November settled 8.5 cents higher at $2.12.
On the KCBT, November closed up by 14.1 cents at $2.201, while deferreds ended three to 10 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.3 cents to 25.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
